title: When the Monsoon Breaks
premise: Quentin Vane, a disgraced mountain guide blacklisted after a client's death he may or may not have caused, is hired by a desperate expedition financier to find the Meridian Survey team that vanished upriver in the Khasra Gorge. Racing the monsoon, Quentin discovers the team alive but fractured — their leader hiding evidence of a mineral strike that governments will kill to control, and among them Elena Marsh, the woman whose testimony once destroyed him. To bring them out, Quentin must choose between exposing the truth that would clear his name and protecting the people who trusted him with it; when the river floods the gorge, he sacrifices his only proof to save them, ending the book cleared of guilt by Elena's confession but poorer than ever — and finally free.
about_author: J. M. Lockridge is the pen name of a former river guide who spent six seasons running commercial expeditions through remote gorge systems before turning to fiction. Lockridge writes adventure novels from a houseboat that migrates between ports, claiming the moving office keeps the plots honest.

chapters.title: The Debt Collector
chapters.summary: Quentin Vane's POV. Broke and blacklisted in a border town, Quentin is cornered by Halvard Reeve, a financier whose survey team has gone silent upriver, and offered a debt-forgiving sum to find them. The emotional beat is reluctant commitment: Quentin recognizes one missing member's name — Elena Marsh — and takes the job for reasons he refuses to examine.

chapters.title: Upstream Silence
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, shifting to Elena's journal entries. Quentin fights upriver through abandoned camps and sabotaged radio gear, finding signs the team didn't vanish — they hid. He locates them at the gorge's forbidden source, where leader Tomas Iriarte guards proof of a mineral strike worth a war. The beat is dread: rescue has become complicity.

chapters.title: What the Source Keeps
chapters.summary: Alternating Quentin and Elena POV. Trapped together by rising water, Elena reveals she testified against Quentin years ago under pressure, believing him negligent; Iriarte plans to sell the strike data to the highest bidder regardless of who dies for it. When Iriarte destroys the boats, Quentin must lead the survivors downriver on foot as the monsoon makes landfall. Climax: betrayal, confession, and the first honest words between Quentin and Elena.

chapters.title: The River Gives Back
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. In the flood's worst hours Quentin abandons his copy of the strike evidence — his leverage, his vindication — to keep an injured porter alive, while Elena carries her own testimony out to the authorities. The beat is hard-won peace: Quentin ends soaked, unpaid, and unburdened, walking out of the gorge beside Elena as the rain finally breaks.
